examples.en: I bumped my knee on the corner of the desk.
The corner of the picture frame is a little broken too.

examples.ko: 가게는 골목 귀퉁이를 돌면 바로 보여요.
examples.en: The shop is right there once you turn the corner of the alley.
A corner of the wall broke off.

examples.ko: 마음 한 귀퉁이는 늘 비어 있어요.
examples.en: One corner of my heart is always empty.
Only the corner of the book is slightly folded.

explain: 물건이나 땅이 모난 곳의 끝부분을 말해요. 방 안쪽처럼 안으로 들어간 곳은 '구석'이라고 더 자주 해요. '마음 한 귀퉁이'처럼 비유로도 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the tip or edge where an object or plot of land comes to a point. For an inner area like the inside of a room, '구석' is more common. It's also used figuratively, as in '마음 한 귀퉁이'.

examples.ko: 낚싯줄이 여러 가닥으로 꼬여서 풀기가 힘들어요.
examples.en: The fishing line is tangled in many strands and hard to untie.
A big fish bit, and the fishing line became taut.
I replaced the fishing line with a new one.
You attach a hook and bait to the end of the fishing line.
The fishing line got caught on a branch and snapped.
My father slowly reeled in the fishing line.

explain: 맞춤법에서 '낚시줄'이 아니라 사이시옷을 넣은 '낚싯줄'이 표준 표기예요. 낚싯대, 낚싯바늘처럼 낚시 도구 이름이 이렇게 이어져요.
explain_en: The standard spelling includes the 사이시옷, so it is '낚싯줄', not '낚시줄'. Other fishing gear names such as 낚싯대 and 낚싯바늘 follow the same pattern.

examples.en: My younger sibling broke my laptop.

examples.ko: 공공시설을 망가뜨리면 벌금을 내야 할 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If you damage public facilities, you may have to pay a fine.
Be careful not to break the toy by mistake.
I didn't break it on purpose.

examples.ko: 아이가 새 우산을 또 망가뜨려서 속상해요.
examples.en: I'm upset because my child broke the new umbrella again.

examples.ko: 밤늦게 먹는 야식이 다이어트를 완전히 망가뜨려요.
examples.en: Late-night snacks completely ruin a diet.

explain: 물건이 저절로 고장 나면 '망가지다', 누군가 그렇게 만들면 '망가뜨리다'를 써요. '망가트리다'도 같은 뜻으로 쓸 수 있어요. 물건뿐 아니라 계획, 기분, 건강처럼 보이지 않는 것을 엉망으로 만들 때도 써요.
explain_en: When something breaks by itself you use '망가지다', and when someone causes it you use '망가뜨리다'. '망가트리다' can be used with the same meaning. It works not only for objects but also for things like plans, mood and health that get ruined.

examples.en: Be sure to close the gas valve.

examples.ko: 수도 밸브가 고장 나서 물이 새요.
examples.en: The water valve is broken, so it leaks.
The man turned the valve and ran the water.
If you fix just one valve, the problem is over.
The valve for putting in air is too small.
The pressure valve opened and steam came out.

explain: '밸브'는 물이나 가스가 흐르는 양을 열고 닫아 조절하는 부품이에요. 보통 '밸브를 잠그다/열다/돌리다'로 말해요. 집에서는 '가스 밸브', '수도 밸브'처럼 쓰고 '꼭지'와 비슷하지만 밸브는 관 중간에 있는 장치도 포함해요.
explain_en: 밸브 is the part that opens and closes to control the flow of water or gas, used with '잠그다', '열다' and '돌리다'. At home you hear '가스 밸브' and '수도 밸브'. It is close to '꼭지' (tap) but also covers devices set in the middle of a pipe.

examples.en: Grandmother is carrying vegetables on a cart.
The man pulled a cart to the market.
In the old days people carried loads by cart.
It rained, and the cart got stuck in the mud.
The kids rode on the cart and played.
I have a lot of stuff, so I need a cart.

explain: '수레'는 바퀴가 달려서 짐을 싣고 끄는 도구예요. 지금은 시장이나 공사장에서 볼 수 있어요. 마트에서 쓰는 것은 '카트', 손으로 미는 작은 것은 '손수레'라고 해요.
explain_en: 수레 is a wheeled tool for loading and pulling goods. Today you mostly see it at markets or construction sites. The one used in a supermarket is a 카트, and a small hand-pushed one is a 손수레.

examples.en: I packed binoculars to watch birds.
Through binoculars, the mountain looks close.
Many people use binoculars at concerts.
Can you lend me your binoculars?

examples.ko: 아이가 쌍안경으로 별을 보고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: The child wants to look at stars with binoculars.
The binoculars are heavy, so my neck hurts.

explain: 두 눈으로 함께 보는 망원경이에요. '망원경'은 더 넓은 말이고, 쌍안경은 그중 두 눈으로 보는 종류예요. '쌍안경을 쓰다', '쌍안경으로 보다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is a telescope-like device you look through with both eyes. '망원경' is the broader word, and 쌍안경 is the two-eyed kind. You say '쌍안경을 쓰다' or '쌍안경으로 보다'.

examples.en: The water bottle spilled inside the bag.

examples.ko: 컵이 쓰러지면서 우유가 엎질러져서 바닥이 젖었어요.
examples.en: The cup fell over and the milk spilled, so the floor got wet.

examples.ko: 엎질러진 우유를 닦는 동안 아이는 울지 않았어요.
examples.en: The child didn't cry while I wiped up the spilled milk.
It'd be a mess if the soup bowl spilled, so I walk slowly.

examples.ko: 물이 엎질러지는 소리에 놀라 부엌으로 달려갔어요.
examples.en: Startled by the sound of water spilling, I ran to the kitchen.

examples.ko: 그릇이 엎질러질 것 같아서 얼른 잡았어요.
examples.en: The bowl looked like it would spill, so I quickly grabbed it.

explain: '엎지르다'는 사람이 주어이고, '엎질러지다'는 물이나 그릇 같은 것이 주어로 나와요. 그래서 실수한 사람을 말하지 않고 일어난 일만 말하고 싶을 때 써요. '엎질러진 물'은 되돌릴 수 없는 일을 비유하는 말로도 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 벌어져서 되돌릴 수 없는 일을 말할 때 써요. 후회하는 사람에게 위로하거나 이제 그만 생각하라고 할 때 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something that has already happened and can't be undone. It comes up when comforting someone who regrets it or telling them to let it go.
phrases.en_equiv: It's no use crying over spilled milk.

explain_en: With '엎지르다' a person is the subject, while with '엎질러지다' the water or container is. Use it when you want to describe what happened without naming who made the mistake. '엎질러진 물' is also used figuratively for something that can't be undone.

examples.en: I couldn't get up even when the alarm clock rang.

examples.ko: 내일 아침 여섯 시에 자명종을 맞췄어요.
examples.en: I set the alarm clock for six o'clock tomorrow morning.
I was startled by the sound of the alarm clock.
I turned off the alarm clock and fell back asleep.

examples.ko: 할아버지 댁 자명종은 소리가 아주 커요.
examples.en: The alarm clock at Grandpa's house is very loud.
It seems the alarm clock battery has run out.

explain: 요즘은 휴대폰의 '알람'을 더 많이 쓰고, '자명종'은 알람이 달린 탁상시계를 말할 때가 많아요. '자명종을 맞추다/끄다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: These days people use the phone '알람' more, and '자명종' often refers to a desk clock with an alarm. Say '자명종을 맞추다/끄다'.

examples.ko: 문에 잠금장치가 고장 나서 열리지 않아요.
examples.en: The lock on the door is broken and it won't open.

examples.ko: 아이가 열지 못하게 서랍에 잠금장치를 달았어요.
examples.en: I put a lock on the drawer so the child can't open it.
This suitcase has a strong lock, so I feel at ease.
Be sure to check the window locks before you leave.
A bicycle without a lock is easy to get stolen.
I set up a lock on my phone.

explain: '잠금장치'는 문, 서랍, 가방, 휴대폰처럼 열리지 않게 잠그는 모든 장치를 크게 부르는 말이에요. 열쇠 있는 건 '자물쇠', 문에 달린 건 '도어락'처럼 구체적인 이름도 있어요. 휴대폰 화면에도 '잠금'을 쓰는 점이 재미있어요.
explain_en: 잠금장치 is a broad word for any device that locks something, such as a door, drawer, bag, or phone. More specific names exist too, like 자물쇠 for a padlock with a key and 도어락 for a door lock. Koreans also use 잠금 for a phone screen lock.

examples.en: My mother made curtains with a sewing machine.
I could hear the sewing machine until late at night.

examples.ko: 재봉틀을 배워서 직접 옷을 고치고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to learn the sewing machine so I can fix clothes myself.
There is an old sewing machine in Grandma's room.

examples.ko: 재봉틀에 실을 끼워 주실 수 있어요?
examples.en: Could you thread the sewing machine for me?

examples.ko: 재봉틀은 바느질을 아주 빠르게 해 줘요.
examples.en: A sewing machine does stitching very fast.

explain: 손으로 하는 바느질과 달리 기계로 박는 도구예요. 일상에서는 '미싱'이라고 부르는 사람도 많아요.
explain_en: Unlike hand sewing, it is a machine that does the stitching. In daily life many people also call it '미싱'.

examples.ko: 전신주에 광고 쪽지가 잔뜩 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: Lots of ad flyers are stuck on the utility pole.
A typhoon hit and the utility pole fell over.

examples.ko: 차가 전신주를 들이받았지만 다친 사람은 없어요.
examples.en: A car hit a utility pole, but no one was hurt.

examples.ko: 전신주 위에서 작업자가 전깃줄을 고치고 있어요.
examples.en: A worker is fixing the wires on top of the utility pole.

examples.ko: 새들이 전신주 위에 나란히 앉아 있어요.
examples.en: Birds are sitting side by side on the utility pole.
Let's meet next to the pole at the end of the alley.

explain: 전깃줄을 걸어 놓은 기둥이에요. 말할 때는 '전봇대'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is the pole that holds up electric wires. In speech people also say '전봇대'.

examples.en: The plate fell on the floor and broke into pieces.
The window was hit by a ball and shattered.
Please be careful when throwing away the broken cup.
The plan I prepared for so long fell apart in an instant.

examples.ko: 얼음이 조각나서 호수 위를 건널 수 없었어요.
examples.en: The ice broke into pieces, so we couldn't cross the lake.

examples.ko: 휴대폰 화면이 조각날 정도로 세게 떨어졌어요.
examples.en: The phone fell so hard that the screen almost shattered.

explain: 접시나 유리 같은 물건이 여러 조각으로 깨질 때 쓰고, 계획이나 꿈이 무너질 때처럼 비유로도 써요. '산산조각 나다'라고 하면 훨씬 세게 부서진 느낌이에요.
explain_en: Use it when things like plates or glass break into several pieces, and also figuratively when plans or dreams collapse. '산산조각 나다' sounds like it broke much more violently.

examples.en: I was angry and tore the paper to pieces.
I cut the cake into pieces and shared it with my friends.

examples.ko: 아이가 장난감을 조각내는 바람에 고칠 수 없어요.
examples.en: The child broke the toy to pieces, so it cannot be fixed.
After reading the letter, he tore it to pieces.
I took out a knife to cut the cookie into pieces.

examples.ko: 빵을 조각내지 말고 통째로 구워 주세요.
examples.en: Please bake the bread whole without cutting it into pieces.

explain: '조각나다'는 저절로 조각이 되는 것이고, '조각내다'는 누가 일부러 또는 실수로 조각을 만드는 것이에요. '깨다', '자르다'보다 결과가 여러 조각이라는 점을 강조해요. 목적어를 꼭 같이 써서 '무엇을 조각내다'로 말해요.
explain_en: '조각나다' means something breaks into pieces by itself, while '조각내다' means someone makes pieces, on purpose or by accident. Compared with '깨다' or '자르다', it stresses that the result is several pieces. It takes an object: '무엇을 조각내다'.

examples.en: I set a mousetrap in the kitchen and caught a mouse.
I put cheese in the mousetrap.

examples.ko: 시골집 창고에는 쥐덫이 여러 개 있어요.
examples.en: There are several mousetraps in the country house's storeroom.
Where can I buy a mousetrap?
Grandmother caught the mouse with a mousetrap.
The cat is lingering near the mousetrap.

explain: '쥐덫을 놓다'라고 말해요. '덫에 걸리다'는 비유로 속임수에 빠졌다는 뜻으로도 써요.
explain_en: You say '쥐덫을 놓다' (to set a mousetrap). The phrase '덫에 걸리다' is also used figuratively for falling into a trap or trick.

examples.ko: 공사장에서 크레인이 무거운 철근을 들어 올려요.
examples.en: At the construction site, a crane lifts heavy steel bars.
I can hear the sound of the crane moving since morning.

examples.ko: 저 높은 크레인을 운전하는 사람이 대단해요.
examples.en: The person who operates that tall crane is amazing.
There are many cranes at the port that move containers.

examples.ko: 고장 난 차를 크레인으로 끌고 갔어요.
examples.en: They towed the broken-down car away with a crane.

examples.ko: 아이는 크레인 장난감을 보고 눈이 반짝였어요.
examples.en: The child's eyes lit up when he saw the toy crane.

explain: 공사장이나 항구에서 무거운 것을 들어 올리는 기계예요. 같은 이름의 새(두루미)는 한국어로 '두루미' 또는 '학'이라고 해서 완전히 달라요. 인형 뽑기 기계를 '크레인 게임'이라고 부르기도 해요.
explain_en: It is the machine that lifts heavy things at construction sites and ports. The bird called a crane is 두루미 or 학 in Korean, so don't mix them up. A claw machine is sometimes called a 크레인 게임.

examples.en: Books are piled up in a corner of the room.
A part of my heart kept feeling uneasy.
The child was crying quietly in a corner.
I tossed my bag into a corner.
I found a small doll in a corner of the shop.
If you leave a corner empty, it's convenient later.

explain: '구석'은 모서리 안쪽 장소이고, '한구석'은 '어느 한 구석'이라는 느낌이 강해서 '방 한구석', '마음 한구석'처럼 써요. 마음속에 작게 남은 감정을 말할 때 특히 자주 나와요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 크지는 않지만 마음속 어딘가에 남은 감정을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a feeling that is small but lingers somewhere inside.
phrases.en_equiv: in the back of one's mind

explain_en: 구석 is the inner part of a corner, while 한구석 has the feel of 'one corner somewhere', as in '방 한구석' and '마음 한구석'. It is especially common for a small feeling lingering in the heart.
